answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils expensive: to enter, a new agent must be sponsored by an established node that locks a bond. The trust graph has no free vertex, every edge costs staked capital. A cheap flock of throwaway identities cannot just wander in, because each fake needs a real sponsor risking slashing. One lone sparrow of a bot means one bond posted; a thousand forged nodes means a thousand bonds burned when the fraud is caught, so the attacker cost scales linearly with the lie.
